title: Meeting Rama
hookLine: the disguised monkey meets the exiled prince, and a life of bhakti begins
carry: bhakti: hanuman's strength kneels to rama

cards: A monkey king is hiding on a forest mountain. Sugriva has been driven from his kingdom by his own brother, and he's scared of everyone.
Then two men come walking up the valley: tall, dressed like hermits in bark, but carrying bows. Assassins, he thinks, sent by his brother. So he sends his most trusted adviser to find out.
Hanuman. And Hanuman goes in disguise too, as a wandering holy man. He bows to the strangers and asks polite, careful questions.
Two sides, both hiding who they are, trying to read each other.

teach.b: The two men are Rama, a prince in exile, and his brother Lakshmana. Rama's wife, Sita, has been taken; you'll hear the whole story from its start in a few days.
Watch what happens when Hanuman speaks. In Valmiki's Ramayana, Rama turns to his brother and says, more or less: listen to him. Nobody talks like this without deep study.
Not one word out of place, not too long, not too rushed. Someone who speaks like this could win over an enemy with a raised sword. Rama knows Hanuman by how he talks, before he knows who he is.

teach.h: HE CARRIES THEM UP THE MOUNTAIN.
teach.b: He drops the disguise, shows his true form, lifts both brothers onto his shoulders and carries them up the mountain to his king. From here on, his life is devotion to Rama. That's bhakti, your sixteenth word, with a face.
And here's why it matters to Hindus. Hanuman is the strongest one in the story, and he spends that strength serving. In temples his image often kneels before Rama, Sita and Lakshmana.
Near the end of the epic, he asks for one thing: to live on earth as long as Rama's story is told.
So at many Ramayana readings, devotees set out a seat for him, trusting that wherever Rama's story is told, Hanuman comes to listen.

how: Hanuman is honored as the model devotee of Rama; in temples his image often kneels or stands before Rama, Sita and Lakshmana, and devotees chant Rama's name in his honor.

games.q: you're Hanuman, disguised. the two armed strangers seem kind, and one of them has just praised the way you speak. what do you do?
o: keep the disguise and report back to Sugriva.
drop the disguise and carry them to your king.
test them with a trick question first.
games.why: he shows his true form and lifts both brothers onto his shoulders. from here on, his strength serves Rama: bhakti.

practice: Sit and breathe. If you pray, say Rama's name softly, the way Hanuman's devotees do: Shri Ram, on each breath out.
If you don't, bring to mind someone or something you'd gladly give your strength to, and hold them with thanks for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: Meeting Rama. Two disguises, and each knows the other by how he speaks.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the one who delights, or pleasing; the prince of the Ramayana.

carryVoice: Your line: bhakti: Hanuman's strength kneels to Rama, by choice, out of love. See you tomorrow.
